title: LanguageDeclaration
description: What a language declares beside its lexicon (lexicons/<lang>/language.yaml; ADR 0145, 0148): the varieties and registers a scope ranges over, the dimensions of each category, the features and values its tokens and lexemes carry, its defaults and its classes. A category is a UD tag: no category system is declared (the owner, round 6). Every statement here is content: drafted `llm:` and REVIEW until signed off.

varieties.description: The varieties a scope may name (ADR 0145), as BCP 47 tags: es-CU, es-ES, apc-LB.

registers.description: The registers a scope may name.

dimensions.description: For each category, the inflectional features every member must choose a value of (ADR 0145: what makes a head a value head). Spanish NOUN: [Number]; apc VERB: [Aspect, Person, Gender, Number].

lexical.description: For each category, the features a member has of itself, the same in all its forms (ADR 0145: a lexical feature; a Spanish noun's gender). A lexeme stores one only where no default gives it, and it is then a part to learn (ADR 0146). A lexeme whose forms name the feature chooses it on its tokens instead (hermano, hermana), which the converter's reports list (docs/migration).

citation.description: For each category, the feature values of the form an entry is spelled in (ADR 0145: the lemma, one of a lexeme's forms by the language's convention): a Spanish verb's infinitive, an apc verb's he-past. A token with these values is written as its entry; every other form is given by a rule, pinned or listed. A feature the lexeme has of itself is left out of its own cell.

bare.description: For each category, the feature values of its form with nothing added: masculine singular for a noun or an adjective, a verb's bare stem (apc: the command to a man). A lexeme the course writes in another form is one it inflects, which a profile's contrast sets marked `inflected` ask (ADR 0081: a slip that trades one agreement ending for another is no typo, on a word that takes them). Where it is the cell an entry is spelled in, it is said here all the same.

features.description: Every feature the language's tokens and lexemes may carry, with its values: UD's names where UD has the feature (Tense: [Past, Pres]), the language's own where it has none.

defaults.description: The language's stated defaults (ADR 0148: a default is a rule; ADR 0146: what one gives is no part of a lexeme). Spanish: a noun in -a is feminine.

classes.description: The language's stated classes (ADR 0148: stated, never counted). A lexeme that belongs to one stores it, and it is a part to learn (ADR 0146).

labels.description: What a learner is shown for a feature value, or for several together where the language has one name for them (ADR 0146: a built gloss is a message over the names of feature values, which are language data). The most specific label whose values a form has names it.

rules.description: The rules the language names and has not written yet (docs/migration-design.md: rules come after the switch, one at a time, each a file of its own with its vectors). A rule named here is its name and what a learner is shown for it: what a `construction:` KC was. A sentence names the ones it is an example of (`uses`), and a node the ones it introduces.

rootClasses.description: The root classes of its bases (docs/rules-design.md, section 3): computed from a base's radicals, never stored. The first whose condition holds is the base's class; one with no condition is the elsewhere class.

stems.description: Its stem templates (docs/rules-design.md, section 2): a base's stem for a stem id, by its Form and root class. Where several fit, the one with the most conditions wins; a stem with no class fits every class its Form has no stem of its own for.

realisation.description: Its realisation rules (ADR 0145; docs/rules-design.md, section 2), in order: the first whose `when` holds of a lexeme and a cell realises it. Each has a rule id, a stem and affix blocks whose exponents are the rule's branches (ADR 0146: a rule's parts).

phonology.description: Its ordered rewrite rules over the whole lexical form, boundaries kept (docs/rules-design.md, section 2): each applied once, in order, at every place it matches.

Notation.title: Notation
Notation.description: What the signs of the language's lexical form are (docs/lexical-forms/<lang>.md), as the rules read them: the vowel signs by name, each long vowel by name, the sign of no vowel, and named sets (UnicodeSets) a rule's pattern names as {name}. A set of marks only is a set of mark sequences; any other set is one of letters.

RootClass.title: RootClass
RootClass.description: One root class: radical `radical` (counted from 1) is in the set `in`, or radicals `same` are one letter; with neither, every base is of it.

Stem.title: Stem
Stem.description: One stem template: a pattern's allomorph (ADR 0145). Digits are the base's radicals; {past} and {present} the short vowel signs of the vowels its Form leaves open, {long past} and {long present} their long vowels (the notation's); everything else is the pattern's own. It fits a base of its Form and class whose radical `radical` is in `in` and whose `vowels` are these, where it says so.

branch.description: Where the template is a thing a learner gets right or wrong of its own (a hollow verb's short past stem), the branch it is of the realisation rule that takes it: rule:apc-perfect|hollow-short.

StemChoice.title: StemChoice
StemChoice.description: Which stem: a stem id; several, the first the base has a template for; or a pattern lexeme's templates (ADR 0145: a value head's pattern).

Branch.title: Branch
Branch.description: A rule's branch: what a learner gets right or wrong of it on its own (ADR 0146). Lower-case ASCII and stable: it enters part ids and card keys (rule:apc-perfect|3fs).

RealisationRule.title: RealisationRule
RealisationRule.description: One realisation rule: where `when` holds of a lexeme and a cell, its stem and then its blocks in order, each adding the most specific exponent whose values the cell has (Pāṇini; Stump's blocks), at most one a block. A prefix goes before what the blocks before it made, a suffix after it.

AffixBlock.title: AffixBlock
AffixBlock.description: One block of exponents: prefixes or suffixes.

Exponent.title: Exponent
Exponent.description: One exponent: the branch it is, the feature values it is for (a comma: one of them; none: elsewhere in its block) and what it adds, in the notation (an affix that begins with a vowel writes it on a carrier, a modifier letter such as the tatweel, and the vowel goes on the letter it joins). It may select the stem.

Rewrite.title: Rewrite
Rewrite.description: One rewrite rule over the whole lexical form (docs/rules-design.md, section 2). Patterns match letters with their sets of marks, never code points in a row: a letter, {set} or [set] of letters, or . (any letter), then its marks exactly (none written: no marks; {set} or [set] of marks: one of them; *: any); + a boundary, +? one or none, # the form's edge (only in `after` and `before`). `to` writes the matched span again: the n-th {set}, [set], ., +? or set of marks of `to` copies the n-th of `find`, and marks written on a copied letter replace its vowel sign. `map` (in place of `to`) maps the letter `find` matches. `after` and `before` are what must stand before and after the span (several: any of them); `at` ties it to the form's start or end.

Context.title: Context
Context.description: What a rewrite's span must stand beside: a pattern, or several of which any will do.

Condition.title: Condition
Condition.description: What a default, an allomorph or (later) a rule's branch looks at in a lexeme or a base (ADR 0148: a rule's conditions). Every key given must hold. A first, small set: it grows with the rule format, which is not designed yet.

ends.description: The lexical form ends in this (Spanish -a; uz -k).

starts.description: The lexical form begins with this.

class.description: It belongs to this class of its language.

endsIn.description: Its lexical form (for an allomorph's `after`, what it follows) ends in what this pattern matches: a rewrite's pattern ({C}: a letter of the notation's set C).

Default.title: Default
Default.description: One default: where `when` holds of a lexeme, it has `gives` unless its entry says otherwise.

notes.description: What a reviewer should know, by support language.

FeatureLabel.title: FeatureLabel
FeatureLabel.description: The name of a set of feature values, by support language: preterite, I (Tense=Past, Person=1, Number=Sing). `pos` narrows it to one category where the same values read otherwise on another.

was.description: The KC whose gloss and notes these were (docs/migration-design.md): kept so a reviewer can trace it. It goes with the switch.

NamedRule.title: NamedRule
NamedRule.description: A rule by its name, with what a learner is shown for it. It says nothing of what the rule does: that is the rule's own file, once it is written.

gloss.description: What a learner is shown for it, by support language (apc used-to: kent + a verb without b-).

was.description: The KC whose gloss and notes these were (docs/migration-design.md): kept so a reviewer can trace it. It goes with the switch.

LexicalClass.title: LexicalClass
LexicalClass.description: One class: a lexical feature a rule reads and no form gives (Spanish e-ie; the -go verbs).

gloss.description: What a learner is shown for it, by support language (pensar: e → ie).

notes.description: What a reviewer should know, by support language.
